Content:
Remember that an outlier of a data set is a value much higher or much lower than the other values.

Content:
When a data set is represented as a dot plot, it's easy to pick out the outliers: we have to look for values much further to the left or right than the main cluster of values.

Content:
To demonstrate, consider the dot plot below:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/e8b2b35105966402658d57ded1e75a17]

Content:
Notice that most values are concentrated between [MATH: 10] and [MATH: 40,] but one value is separated from the main group.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/3681a7fc2bbbc34826ce5d58e6e4199e]

Content:
Since this value is separated from the main group, we conclude that [MATH: {\color{blue}100}] is an outlier of the distribution.

Content:
When a distribution is perfectly symmetric, the mean lies at the midpoint of the distribution.

Content:
To demonstrate, consider the symmetric distribution below:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/be71af1c222f92a6ec66fe870e203217]

Content:
To calculate this distribution's mean (midpoint), we find the mean of the two most extreme values. The largest value is [MATH: 70], and the smallest value is [MATH: 10.] Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: mean|= (10 + 70)/(2); = (80)/(2); = 40.]

Content:
Also, when a distribution is perfectly symmetric, the mean and the median are equal. Therefore, for the dataset above, we have
[MATH: \textrm{median} = 40.]

items.title: Calculating Mean and Median for Symmetric Data Sets

sections.normalized_html: Find the mean and median of the dataset shown above.
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/8eea1d1cfe3c11b1ce71cf5760a1a016]

Find the mean and median of the dataset shown above.

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Recall that when a distribution is perfectly symmetric,

  • the mean and the median are equal, and

  • the mean (and median) lie at the midpoint of the distribution.

Notice that this dataset is symmetric.

To calculate the mean (midpoint) of this distribution, we find the mean of the two most extreme values. The largest value is [MATH: 55], and the smallest value is [MATH: 20.] Therefore,

[MATH: \textrm{mean} = \dfrac{55+20}{2} = \dfrac{75}{2} = 37.5.]

Therefore, the mean is [MATH: 37.5] and the median is [MATH: 37.5.]

items.title: Estimating the Location of the Mean From a Dot Plot

sections.normalized_html:
The dot plot above shows how much time each student in Mr. Johnson's class spent studying math on a particular day. Each dot represents a single student.

Which of the following statements are true?

  1. The distribution is approximately symmetric.

  2. The mean of the distribution equals [MATH: 20\, \text{min}.]

  3. The mean of the distribution exceeds [MATH: 20 \, \text{min}.]

  4. The mean of the distribution is less than [MATH: 20 \, \text{min}.]
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/f3d79d33e8c845f478bb12d7d7ff172e]

The dot plot above shows how much time each student in Mr. Johnson's class spent studying math on a particular day. Each dot represents a single student.

Which of the following statements are true?

1. The distribution is approximately symmetric.
2. The mean of the distribution equals [MATH: 20\, \text{min}.]
3. The mean of the distribution exceeds [MATH: 20 \, \text{min}.]
4. The mean of the distribution is less than [MATH: 20 \, \text{min}.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Let's examine the statements one by one.

  • Statement I is false. The distribution is left-skewed (since we have a longer tail on the left). It is not symmetric.

  • Statement III is true, while statements II and IV are false. All of the data is situated between [MATH: 5] and [MATH: 35] minutes. If the data were symmetric, then the mean would be given by the midpoint, which is [MATH: \dfrac{5+35}{2} = 20 \, \text{min}.] However, since the distribution is left-skewed, most of the data points are concentrated on the right-hand side. This indicates that the mean of our distribution lies to the right of the midpoint.

    So, the mean is greater than [MATH: 20] minutes.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

Item 5 — Tutorial: Tails, Skew, and Symmetry

Content:
A tail of a distribution is a part that extends away from the main cluster.

Content:
If the left tail of the distribution is longer than the right tail, then we say that the distribution is left-skewed (or negatively skewed). An example of a left-skewed distribution is shown below.

Graphic:

Graphic:

Item 9 — Tutorial: The Mean and Median of a Symmetric Distribution

Content:
When a distribution is perfectly symmetric, the mean lies at the midpoint of the distribution.

Content:
To demonstrate, consider the symmetric distribution below:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/be71af1c222f92a6ec66fe870e203217]

Content:
To calculate this distribution's mean (midpoint), we find the mean of the two most extreme values. The largest value is [MATH: 70], and the smallest value is [MATH: 10.] Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: mean|= (10 + 70)/(2); = (80)/(2); = 40.]

Content:
Also, when a distribution is perfectly symmetric, the mean and the median are equal. Therefore, for the dataset above, we have
[MATH: \textrm{median} = 40.]

Notice that this dataset is symmetric.

To calculate the mean (midpoint) of this distribution, we find the mean of the two most extreme values. The largest value is [MATH: 55], and the smallest value is [MATH: 20.] Therefore,

[MATH: \textrm{mean} = \dfrac{55+20}{2} = \dfrac{75}{2} = 37.5.]

Therefore, the mean is [MATH: 37.5] and the median is [MATH: 37.5.]

Item 14 — Example: Estimating the Location of the Mean From a Dot Plot

Example Prompt:
[IMG: /graphics/f3d79d33e8c845f478bb12d7d7ff172e]

The dot plot above shows how much time each student in Mr. Johnson's class spent studying math on a particular day. Each dot represents a single student.

Which of the following statements are true?

1. The distribution is approximately symmetric.
2. The mean of the distribution equals [MATH: 20\, \text{min}.]
3. The mean of the distribution exceeds [MATH: 20 \, \text{min}.]
4. The mean of the distribution is less than [MATH: 20 \, \text{min}.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Let's examine the statements one by one.

- Statement I is false. The distribution is left-skewed (since we have a longer tail on the left). It is not symmetric.

[IMG: /graphics/260396ec50981425c4f6da587e4b7319]

- Statement III is true, while statements II and IV are false. All of the data is situated between [MATH: 5] and [MATH: 35] minutes. If the data were symmetric, then the mean would be given by the midpoint, which is
[MATH: \dfrac{5+35}{2} = 20 \, \text{min}.]
However, since the distribution is left-skewed, most of the data points are concentrated on the right-hand side. This indicates that the mean of our distribution lies to the right of the midpoint.

[IMG: /graphics/664be3a6bbcfe33007a8fe4898ca0d58]

So, the mean is greater than [MATH: 20] minutes.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
